name: High-ticket dropshipping in a niche (camper van accessories)
one_liner: An e-commerce store that sells £1,000+ products from existing brands on dropship or reseller terms, without making its own products.
customer: Hobbyists buying expensive gear, e.g. van-life and campervan owners
offer: A curated online store for high-ticket accessories from established brands
how_it_makes_money: The margin on each sale: $150 to several thousand dollars of profit per order on products priced $1,000+. The case grew to $40k/month while the founder kept a day job, then to $120k/month in sales.
startup_cost: low (no stated amount; no inventory because brands already have demand and stock)
evidence: 'e-commerce store selling camper van accessories to 40 grand a month, while still working his day job' (Je0NxaeOYFI)
'grown to $120,000 a month in sales... by partnering with brands that already had demand' (Je0NxaeOYFI)
'products that are retailing for $1,000 plus... $150 up to a few thousand dollars of profit in every sale' (Je0NxaeOYFI)
'I got four brands for my site when I started' (Je0NxaeOYFI)
risks: Brands may refuse to work with a new store
Paid traffic costs can eat the margin
High-value orders mean customer service and returns work
The founder says it is 'not passive'

name: Niche dictation/utility app for an underserved user
one_liner: A simple app in a crowded category, built for a specific group for whom it solves a real problem rather than being a nice-to-have.
customer: An overlooked user group (the case started as a tool for the founder's dad) that needs the tool to work
offer: A dictation app, first a Chrome extension and later on Windows, Mac, Linux, iOS and Android
how_it_makes_money: Software revenue of $16–20k/month (the pricing model is not stated in the digest)
time_to_first_revenue: Launched about 2 years ago; people downloaded it without marketing
evidence: 'launched it two years ago as a Chrome extension... built it as a fun tool for my dad' (LrLDsvbdPr0)
'to the people that I'm serving, it's a pain killer' (LrLDsvbdPr0)
risks: The market is saturated, with competitors that have raised millions
Distribution depends on finding the specific group
Needs software skills or AI-assisted building
Supporting many platforms adds maintenance work

name: Inflatable outdoor/indoor movie night rentals
one_liner: Renting inflatable cinema screens with setup for school, HOA, community and private events.
customer: Schools, HOAs (resident associations), parents and event organisers
offer: A movie-night package: inflatable screen, projector, sound, seating, and setup
how_it_makes_money: A booking fee per event. The case did $10k of bookings in one week, is targeting about $100k a year, and claims 80% margins.
startup_cost: low ($250–300 first screen from Amazon; later a 20-foot commercial screen)
time_to_first_revenue: Days: the first booking came from a Facebook Marketplace listing before he felt prepared
evidence: 'I did 10,000 in sales in bookings... last week' (LGkcTUfySDU)
'His first screen cost about 300 bucks on Amazon' (LGkcTUfySDU)
'working towards 100 grand this year at 80% profit margins' (LGkcTUfySDU)
risks: Delivery is in person, so it is not async
UK weather and wind (he had trouble in 10 mph wind)
Needs insurance and screening licences for public showings

name: Reselling underpriced secondhand goods (incl. niche electronics/cables)
one_liner: Buying items that are undervalued at car boot sales, charity shops and liquidations, then reselling them on eBay or Marketplace.
customer: Online buyers looking for working products at about 50% off new
offer: Used or surplus goods, e.g. obsolete AV cables and VCRs, and bulk lots
how_it_makes_money: Buy low, sell high. Cables bought for $1 sell for about $60. One bulk deal made $3–5k net from 15 hours of work. The business crossed six figures in revenue, at roughly $10–20k a month.
startup_cost: low (cash for stock; a few hundred to start)
time_to_first_revenue: Days ('you go and buy an item and then the next day it's sold')
evidence: 'after 15 hours of combined work you make 3,000 to 5,000 in net profit' (KjTHJ740fCY)
'thrift stores... throw them in the cord bucket for a dollar and they sell for like 60 bucks on eBay' (KjTHJ740fCY)
'anyone can make an extra 1,000 to $5,000 a month... two to five hours a week' (KjTHJ740fCY)
risks: Sourcing takes physical time and is hard to scale
Selling regularly brings in HMRC trading-income reporting

name: DTC subscription for a boring replenishable product
one_liner: Selling a consumable household product online, direct to the customer, where buying it today is a poor experience.
customer: Homeowners who need regular replacements (air filters in the case)
offer: Replacement consumables, e.g. HVAC air filters, sold online and on subscription
how_it_makes_money: Repeat orders and subscriptions. Filterbuy does about $25M/month, but that is at manufacturing scale after buying a business.
startup_cost: high at the case's scale ($1.5M debt to buy a business making $300k/year); a reseller version would be low to medium
evidence: 'We manufacture about 150,000 air filters a day and do roughly $25 million a month' (Kxu4icXtNcU)
'chose based on which boring product would still exist in 20 years... existing customer experience wasn't particularly good' (Kxu4icXtNcU)
risks: Evidence for a small solo version is weak because the case is a large manufacturer
Hard to compete with commodity prices
